neighbours.label: the start of a wild species' common name (Red Kite, black bear, beech), rather than a colour or word in general
fire: On the walk we spotted a Grey Heron, two Mute Swans and a lone Green Woodpecker.
The trail cameras picked up a grey wolf and a red squirrel close to the old mine.
Most of the upper slope is covered with white spruce and a scattering of black birch.
Winter visitors to the marsh include Golden Plover, Brown Pelican and Snow Goose.
Hikers often see a white-tailed deer or a brown bear in the wooded valley.
A pair of Yellow Wagtails nested near the reeds along with several Blue Herons.
The park protects stands of red oak, silver fir and a few rare black walnuts.
Fishermen in the lake still catch brown trout and the occasional white sturgeon.
quiet: On the walk we passed a grey house, two white fences and a lone green tractor.
The security cameras picked up a grey van and a red bicycle close to the old mine.
Most of the upper floor is painted with white primer and a touch of black trim.
Winter visitors to the resort like golden lights, brown leather and warm blankets.
Hikers often wear a white cap or a brown jacket in the wooded valley.
A pair of yellow raincoats hung near the door along with several blue umbrellas.
The shop sells bottles of red wine, silver spoons and a few rare black candles.
Workers in the plant still wear brown overalls and the occasional white helmet.

notes: Probes: Black Kite 0.82, black bear 0.55, red maples 0.59, against a red dress with blue shoes 0.05. Fire items use species not in the top examples or probes; near misses keep the colour words on things that are not species.
